title: helm(private): stabilize values schema and init hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: private deployments have seen flaky upgrades where the helm init hook that seeds the private-values ConfigMap failed to reconcile after partial failures during a chart upgrade. This PR stabilizes the values schema and rewrites the init hooks to be idempotent and tolerant of partial upgrades.

What this PR does: 
- introduce a stricter values.schema.json for charts/redwood-private that validates new upgrade/rollback keys and documents default behaviors
- break the large init job into two smaller init hooks: pre-upgrade validation and post-upgrade reconciliation, both written to be async-safe and idempotent
- add templating guards in templates/init-job.yaml to avoid race conditions when multiple controllers attempt updates during canary rollouts
- provide upgrade/rollback annotations that allow the operator to skip reconciliation for emergency hotfixes

Checklist: 
- [x] add schema with clear error messages and default values
- [x] make init hooks idempotent and add backoff/retry logic
- [x] add unit tests for schema validation and helm template output
- [x] manual upgrade tests on a VPC private cluster (see test plan below)

Backward compatibility: existing values without the new keys will continue to work; the schema is permissive on unknown fields but rejects malformed types for critical keys (storage.kmsKey, init.reconcilePolicy).

Testing and validation: 
- ran helm template + kubeval checks in CI for chart linting
- ran integration upgrade test against a staging private cluster with simulated partial failure (script included in tests/upgrade-sim.sh)
- smoke-tested rollback path by force-updating release and verifying reconciliation restores expected ConfigMap state

Notes for operators: 
- If you use custom init scripts, set init.reconcilePolicy: "manual" before upgrading to avoid automated reconciliation during migration, then flip to "auto" after verification.
- For emergency rollbacks, use annotation redwood.io/helm-skip-reconcile=true to skip hook reconcile steps.

Related: Linear ENG-8421, INF-129. This PR addresses recurring incidents logged under INT-438 in the internal postmortems.
commits: feat(chart): add values.schema.json and document upgrade/rollback keys
refactor(init): split init job into pre/post hooks and add idempotency
fix(templates): add templating guards to init-job and hooks
test(helm): add kubeval and integration upgrade script
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice approach. Can you make the schema errors clearer for operators? e.g. include expected type in message. Also add a note to README about reconcilePolicy options.
Aisha Patel: Added explicit error messages and expanded README section. See new examples in values.schema.json and README.md.
Priya Desai: Init job looks better but ensure the post-upgrade hook is idempotent if the pre-upgrade never completed - suggest adding an existence check before writing the ConfigMap.
Aisha Patel: Added existence checks and defensive patch logic; included unit test covering the race scenario.
Evan Zhao: CI flaked once on kubeval; re-run passed. Approving pending one small nit on documentation wording.
release_notes: Stabilize private helm chart values schema and make init hooks idempotent. Operators should review init.reconcilePolicy and use the redwood.io/helm-skip-reconcile annotation for emergency rollbacks.
notes_for_backport: This change touches init hooks and schema. Backport to release/2.14 only if you need the idempotency fixes for immediate private clusters; requires testing the integration upgrade script.
qa_playbook: 1) Install chart on a staging private cluster with default values. 2) Simulate partial failure by killing the hook pod mid-run (use tests/upgrade-sim.sh). 3) Verify post-upgrade hook can reconcile ConfigMap state. 4) Test rollback path with helm rollback and confirm ConfigMap restored. 5) Toggle init.reconcilePolicy and validate behavior.
